history.p: The "Michel Angelo" overture was written shortly after the "Hamlet" overture. Within two months after the first performance in Copenhagen, it had also been performed in Leipzig, Dresden and Köln. Until Gade's death in 1890 was performed more than hundred times.

physDesc.physMedium: 1 single folio. Written in ink. Paper: 20 staves. Notated on two staves. With numerous cancellations.

Enclosed in a folder bound in white silk, front embroidered in gold with a crown and a flower stem. On the right page of inside spread is a picture of Gade as a conductor, not known from other sources. Written in ink. Paper: 16 staves. Paginated 1-38. At the end of the music "Fine / Kjøbenh. 1861" and Gade's musical signature.

event.desc: The manuscript was donated to Queen Louise after Gade's death and transferred to The Royal Library
